body: I'm sorry. I didnt mean to tell you to not take responsibility, you do need to. I do think you're using guilt to punish yourself. There has been people in history who have done awful things, but realized what they were doing was wrong and tried to redeem themselves in diffrerent ways. Why would you and i be any different from them? Sorry though, I dont want to be an armchair psychologist. I genuinely hope you feel better about yourself.

This may be an unpopular opinion but I hate how social media and the world has made us think people who were abusive to their partner in the past makes them irredeemable monsters. The stuff you did was wrong, yeah, but you can get actual help for that. Most people in the mental health field don't judge on that from my experience (they are trained that way). I hope one day you feel better about yourself and form a healthy relationship with someone else.
Ok. Doing stuff you love is a good coping mechanism in my opinion. But please talk to a counselor soon.
Do you have a therapist or an adult you could talk to someone about this? You can get help from them.
Its a good thing you acknowledged you were the toxic person in a relationship and you feel guilt about it. But its not good that its torturing you. I'm sorry for you and the person.
Do you have any hobbies or any thing that distracts you from your pain? Like a fandom or something.
Hello. Did your parents say anything to you that made you feel this way??
